recommendation: Keep the source fix. It completes FHIR-20390 in the current core HTTP source without duplicating the already-audited FHIR-26688 and FHIR-36859 decisions. Any future discussion about the one-match 201 Created response text should be handled as a separate issue.
issue_request: FHIR-20390 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core-http. It asked what "id provided" means in a conditional update, noted ambiguity between Resource.id and an _id search parameter, and approved changing the bullets to say Resource.id while removing the sentence saying a supplied id is ignored.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-20390 was found. GF#17906 introduced the split conditional update decision table in source/http.html, FHIR-26688 removed the contradictory ignore-id sentence, and FHIR-36859 later split the no-match/id-provided behavior. The Jira comment saying changes were applied with FHIR-31965 appears to refer to the same HTTP-page application period, but the FHIR-31965 source commit itself changed conditional create response metadata rather than this wording.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active core HTTP narrative page, with publish.ini mapping http.html to the built HTTP page. FHIR-26688 and FHIR-36859 are already represented on the combined branch, so this reconciliation preserved their semantics and only completed the Resource.id wording clarification. The relevant Zulip thread confirmed the ambiguity was specifically Resource.id versus _id and supported deleting the ignore-id sentence.
reconciliation: Updated source/http.html conditional update bullets from bare "id provided" / "resource id provided" labels to Resource.id labels, including clearer no-match wording for whether a resource already exists with that id. This preserves the existing Update as Create, 409 Conflict, one-match update, and mismatching-id 400 Bad Request outcomes.
source_changes: source/http.html: clarified conditional update branch labels to use Resource.id and to distinguish no-match cases by whether a resource already exists with that id.

related_jiras.note: Introduced the conditional update decision table with the id-provided shorthand later clarified by FHIR-20390.

Split the no-match/Resource.id-provided branch into non-existing-id and existing-id outcomes; already represented on the combined branch and preserved by this edit.
Mentioned in the FHIR-20390 Jira application comment, but its source commit addressed conditional create response metadata rather than this conditional update Resource.id wording.
